title: Q:rods-matching-o - do heritable bit-string kinds on the Marangoni rods, interacting through a matching kernel, keep producing new adaptive kinds the way coevbits predators do, with bodies, division and death that are not agent rules?
summary: coevbits (20261026T0735-c38-coevbits-predator-o, replicated and robust) shows that an inescapable matching target sustains adaptive novelty, but its individuals, division and death are agent rules, so it cannot give C:open-ended (IDHO). The two-kind Marangoni rods (20261026T0630-c34-marangoni-two-kinds, 20261026T0655-c34-two-kinds-swap) already carry a heritable kind through fission with 0 conversions. Proposal: give each rod a short genotype (k-bit vector carried as k surfactant channels with majority feedback, as in two-kinds) and an interaction that depends on matching: when two rods touch, the rod whose genotype matches the other's within w bits gains the other's matter (a capture through a local exchange term exp(-h^2/w^2), h computed from the contact's channel compositions), so one lineage eats another. Mutation is noise on the channels at fission. Controls: the constant-exchange twin (exchange independent of h) and the time-shift profile.
experiment: One loop: k=4 channels (16 kinds) on the two-kinds rod world, 192^2, T=3000, 2 seeds plus the constant-exchange twin; measure kind shares over time, X events (matter transfer on contact) and the time-shift capture profile on kind censuses every 100 t; success = a dip after lag 0 absent in the twin.
